links.outcome: Perceived workflow disruption of PACS-integrated AI vs non-integrated ESDR tool
links.effect: 93.3% (14/15) said PACS-integrated AI did not interfere with practice; 55.6% (5/9) said the non-integrated ESDR tool imposed substantial burden; only 28% complete referral records and 44.4% reviewed feedback.
links.quote: However, 55.6% (5/9) of respiratory physicians indicated that the ESDR tool imposed a substantial burden on daily tasks.

openai.sample_unit: patients across postimplementation (1375) and historical-control (1591) periods
models_evaluated: HY Medical Technology Co., Ltd. AI-assisted pulmonary nodule screening system

links.outcome: Completion and timeliness of structured referral following AI-assisted screening
links.effect: Referral completion was 88% (22/25); the median interval from referral submission to hospital visit was 3 (IQR 2‐4) days. Referral outcomes lacked a historical comparison.
links.quote: At the patient level, of the 25 individuals who consented to referral, 22 successfully completed the referral process by visiting the tertiary hospital, yielding a referral completion rate of 88%.

links.outcome: Clinician burden and workflow disruption associated with a separate referral-data platform
links.effect: ESDR-related burden was reported by 55.6% (5/9) of secondary-hospital respiratory physicians; 62.5% (5/8) at the tertiary hospital reported workflow disruptions associated with external platform access.
links.quote: However, 55.6% (5/9) of respiratory physicians indicated that the ESDR tool imposed a substantial burden on daily tasks.

links.outcome: Successful automated transfer of CT images and AI results between hospitals
links.effect: CT image transmission succeeded for 90.9% (20/22); two patients experienced PACS-related transmission failures and were required to carry physical CT films to the tertiary hospital.
links.quote: Despite a relatively high CT image transmission success rate of 90.9% (20/22), system-level failures persisted.

unlisted_practices: Waiving tertiary-care registration fees and providing appointment scheduling and navigation support for referred patients.
Returning specialist diagnoses and follow-up recommendations to referring clinicians through a bidirectional interhospital feedback platform.

models_evaluated: HY Medical Technology AI-assisted pulmonary nodule diagnostic software

links.effect: 55.6% (5/9) of secondary hospital respiratory physicians reported the external system imposed a substantial burden on daily tasks.
links.quote: The primary challenge was the lack of interoperability between the ESDR system and the hospital’s internal information systems, which required physicians to manually access the platform via an external web link to upload or retrieve patient data.

links.effect: Two of the 22 successfully referred patients experienced data transmission failures that prevented the upload of AI-generated results and images.
links.quote: Among the 22 patients who successfully completed the referral process, two experienced data transmission failures due to PACS system malfunctions at the secondary hospital, which prevented the upload of AI-generated results and CT images to the ESDR platform.

unlisted_practices: establishing interhospital referral networks for patients flagged by AI screening
providing downstream tertiary diagnostic feedback to primary/secondary AI users to assess performance

screen.reason: This prospective process evaluation tests a real-world implementation strategy (including structured referral mechanisms, cloud-based data transfer, and feedback systems) for AI-assisted CT lung nodule screening in a hospital, evaluating RE-AIM outcomes.
